elements.manual_reason: Only candidate is the whole-frame diff box (b01, used for the grid); the selected host hex that turns purple at the end has no own box.
elements.label: Selected host hexagon highlight

sfx_review.label: music
sfx_review.note: Vertical broadband streak is one of an evenly spaced train of percussion hits through the whole window (same shape before and after); part of the music bed, not a chime tied to the zoom.

pattern.description: Starting tight on a few large host hexagons, the host map zooms out continuously until thousands of tiny hexes fill the frame; the host-detail panel stays fixed while the selected host is marked purple on landing.
pattern.why_premium: One unbroken zoom turns a single host into a fleet of 7,061, showing scale through motion instead of a number, while the fixed detail panel keeps the viewer anchored.

build_hint.gsap: gsap.fromTo('.hostmap', {scale: 8, transformOrigin: '50% 40%'}, {scale: 1, duration: 0.6, ease: 'power2.inOut'}); detail panel stays static on a separate layer; at the end tl.set('.hex-selected', {backgroundColor: '#8e44ad'}) (or a 0.1 s fade).
build_hint.remotion: scale = interpolate(frame, [0, 36], [8, 1], {easing: Easing.inOut(Easing.cubic), extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}) on the map layer with transformOrigin '50% 40%'; detail panel outside the scaled layer; selected hex colour switches at the last frame.

notes: Camera verdict is pull_out; a near-cut energy spike near the start suggests the first filmstrip frame (with chips inside big hexes) may belong to a cut into the zoom. Pattern is a reverse of ui_camera_push_in, so proposed as 'other'.
